title: Contact Lenses vs Glasses | Northgate Eyecare
question: Are daily disposable contact lenses better than monthly lenses?

passages.heading: Contact Lenses vs Glasses | Northgate Eyecare
Contact lens options
passages.text: We fit soft daily disposables, soft monthly lenses, toric lenses for astigmatism, multifocal contacts for over-40s, and rigid gas permeable lenses for keratoconus and irregular corneas.

passages.heading: Dailies compared with monthlies
passages.text: Daily disposables are opened fresh each morning and thrown out at night — no cleaning solution, no case, and the lowest risk of deposit build-up and lens-related infection, which makes them our usual recommendation for part-time wear, sport, travel and hay fever season. Monthly lenses cost less per day of wear if you wear lenses every day, and a wider range of prescriptions and designs is available in monthly, including most complex torics. The trade-off is that monthlies require nightly cleaning and disinfecting and must be replaced strictly on schedule. For a full-time wearer with a straightforward prescription, monthlies are usually the more economical choice; for anyone wearing lenses two or three days a week, dailies work out cheaper and safer.

passages.heading: Contact lens fittings
passages.text: A fitting appointment includes corneal measurements, a trial pair, teaching you insertion and removal, and a follow-up check two weeks later to confirm the fit and your comfort.

title: Vestibular Rehabilitation | Coastline Physio & Rehab
question: How many sessions of vestibular rehab will I need for BPPV?

passages.heading: Dizziness and vertigo
passages.text: Vertigo is the sensation that you or the room is spinning. The most common cause is benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), where crystals in the inner ear move into a balance canal and send false signals to the brain about head position.

passages.heading: Assessment
passages.text: Our vestibular-trained physiotherapists use the Dix-Hallpike and roll tests with infrared goggles to identify which canal is involved. We also screen your neck, eye movements and balance to rule out other causes of dizziness.

passages.heading: Treatment
passages.text: BPPV is treated with repositioning manoeuvres such as the Epley, performed in the clinic, which guide the displaced crystals back out of the canal. Most people notice a marked change in their symptoms quite quickly. We follow up with gaze stabilisation and balance retraining exercises to do at home, and we retest at your next visit to confirm the canal has cleared. Occasionally symptoms recur and further treatment is needed.

passages.heading: Booking
passages.text: Vestibular assessments are booked as an extended initial appointment. Please arrange a lift home, as you may feel briefly unsteady after a manoeuvre.

why: BPPV treatment is described in clinical detail but the page only says symptoms change "quite quickly" and may recur, never giving a session count, so the count fact is absent.

passages.heading: Switching Your Payroll to Ashworth Payroll Bureau
Moving mid-year is easier than you think
passages.text: Most employers assume they are locked in until 6 April. In practice we take on payrolls in every month of the tax year, and as long as we have accurate year-to-date figures there is no disruption to your employees or to your RTI record.

passages.text: 1. Discovery call. We agree your pay frequencies, payment dates, cut-off dates and who authorises each run. 2. Data collection. You send us your most recent FPS submission, employee year-to-date figures, starter and leaver paperwork and your pension scheme details. 3. Parallel run. Lifespan
passages.text: A standing seam metal roof installed over synthetic underlayment will last 40 to 70 years here. passages.text: Standing seam runs $1,200 to $1,800 per roofing square installed. Architectural shingles run $450 to $650 per square. Metal costs roughly two to three times as much on day one.

passages.text: Metal dents but rarely leaks after a hail event, so carriers often write cosmetic-damage exclusions on metal. Shingles bruise and lose granules, which is a covered loss on most policies.

title: Apex Auto Spa — Paint Decontamination Explained
question: what is a clay bar treatment
why: The page gives a plain definitional statement of what a clay bar is and what it removes, so the term is defined rather than merely mentioned.

passages.heading: Apex Auto Spa — Paint Decontamination Explained
What a Clay Bar Actually Does
passages.text: A clay bar is a pliable block of engineered resin that you glide across lubricated paint. Washing lifts what sits on top of the clear coat; claying shears off what has bonded into it — rail dust, industrial fallout, overspray, tree sap and brake particles. Run a hand over a car that has never been decontaminated and it feels like fine sandpaper. Clay the same panel and it feels like glass.

passages.heading: When a Clay Treatment Is Needed
passages.text: Most cars want a clay treatment once or twice a year. If you are about to polish or install a coating, decontamination is not optional — anything left bonded to the paint gets sealed under the new layer or dragged across it by the pad.

passages.heading: Chemical Decontamination First
passages.text: Before we clay, we spray an iron remover that dissolves embedded ferrous particles and bleeds purple as it works. Doing the chemical stage first means less mechanical work on the paint, and less mechanical work means fewer marks to polish out afterwards.
